categories.title: Self-hosting
categories.scope: servers, reverse proxies, remote access, monitoring and household apps you run yourself

categories.title: Home automation
categories.scope: hubs, device bridges, cameras and automations that run locally

categories.title: Local AI and agents
categories.scope: model runners and servers, coding agents, agent frameworks and evaluation
categories.note: Agents run code and edit files with your access. Read the code, pin a version and give them the least access that works; the [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies. A code license says nothing about model weights; read each model card.

categories.title: Agent memory
categories.scope: memory layers, knowledge graphs and context stores that keep what an agent learned across sessions
categories.note: A memory layer stores what your agents read and say. Most send that text to a hosted model for extraction and embeddings by default, and several send usage telemetry; set local models and turn telemetry off before adding private data. The [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies.

categories.title: MCP servers and SDKs
categories.scope: Model Context Protocol servers, SDKs, gateways and debuggers that connect AI tools to other software
categories.note: **Every MCP server runs code on your machine with the access you give it.** Read the code, pin a version, keep it local, and apply the [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) before connecting one to an agent.

categories.title: Agent skills and instruction files
categories.scope: instruction files, skills and plugins that change how a coding agent works
categories.note: A skill is instructions your agent follows with your access, and some plugins add hooks that run at every session start. Read it before installing, install from a reviewed commit rather than a branch, and check each skill's license: one repository can mix licenses. The [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies.

categories.title: Speech
categories.scope: speech-to-text and text-to-speech that run locally
categories.note: A code license says nothing about model weights or voices, which often carry their own terms; read each model card. Clone a voice only with its owner's consent.

categories.title: Developer tools and security
categories.scope: package managers, linters, scanners, supply-chain checks and command-line tools

entries.name: thedotmack/claude-mem
entries.why: Records what a coding agent does each session, compresses it with a model and injects the relevant parts into later sessions, for several agent CLIs.
entries.note: the installer asks you to sign in to the vendor's hosted memory; pass an explicit `--provider` or set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false` to stay local; it stores what your agent reads and does, so keep private work out of it until you have read where that goes

entries.name: mem0ai/mem0
entries.why: Memory layer that extracts facts from agent conversations into a vector store for later sessions; runs locally once the model and embedder are set.
entries.note: sends usage events (versions, operating system, provider names, memory IDs, hashed user IDs) to PostHog by default until `MEM0_TELEMETRY=false` is set; the default LLM and embedder are OpenAI, so set both to local ones to keep memory text on your machine; the default vector store path is under /tmp, so set a lasting one; graph memory, temporal search and decay are hosted-platform features, not in the open-source package

entries.name: vectorize-io/hindsight
entries.why: Self-hosted agent memory server that merges retained facts in the background into sourced observations; serves recall and reflect over REST and MCP.
entries.note: the server's default model provider is OpenAI, and the coding-agents installer and most framework integrations default to the vendor's hosted API; the coding-agents installer also seeds memory from a repository's git history on first run by default; set a local model provider and a localhost server URL, and pin a release tag, before first use

entries.name: topoteretes/cognee
entries.why: Turns documents and conversations into a knowledge graph plus a vector index; its default stores are embedded files, so it needs no database server.
entries.note: sends usage events by default, including a machine ID kept in `~/.cognee` that survives reinstalls, until `TELEMETRY_DISABLED` is set; with an `LLM_API_KEY` it uses OpenAI for extraction and embeddings, and without one it extracts with a local model and installs PyTorch itself on first use unless `GLINER_AUTO_INSTALL=false` is set or the `gliner` extra was installed; the Postgres graph store is a demo, and its production version is a separate licensed product

entries.name: getzep/graphiti
entries.why: Builds a knowledge graph from agent conversations and keeps a validity window on each fact, so a replaced fact is marked instead of deleted.
entries.note: sends anonymous usage statistics to PostHog by default until `GRAPHITI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` is set; defaults to OpenAI for extraction, embeddings and reranking, so point it at a local OpenAI-compatible server before adding private data; needs a Neo4j server (GPL-3.0), FalkorDB (SSPL-1.0, source-available) or Amazon Neptune, and its bundled MCP server defaults to FalkorDB; search does not drop facts marked invalid unless you pass a date filter

entries.name: garrytan/gbrain
entries.why: Agent memory in which every fact keeps its source and can be corrected or withdrawn; starts as a keyless local brain with cloud embeddings opt-in.
entries.note: memories an agent saves are visible to every connected agent by default; pass `visibility: "private"` for local-only facts; API keys, automatic capture and paid enrichment are separate opt-ins

entries.name: AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian
entries.why: Keeps an agent's knowledge as a plain Markdown Obsidian vault: drop in a source and the agent reads, links and files it in files you own.

entries.name: breferrari/obsidian-mind
entries.why: An Obsidian vault as agent memory, filled automatically by agent hooks at session start, prompt, tool use, compaction and stop, with local semantic search; read what its hooks do before adding them beside your own.

entries.name: volcengine/OpenViking
entries.why: Context server that keeps agent memory, documents and skills as a virtual filesystem, with short summaries an agent reads before the source.
entries.note: crates/ (ov_cli, ragfs) and examples/ are Apache-2.0; the whole repository was Apache-2.0 through v0.2.14 (2026-03-30) and is AGPL-3.0 from the v0.2.15 tag on; embeddings default to Volcengine's hosted service until another provider is configured; a paid edition is unlocked by a license key

entries.name: mattpocock/skills

entries.name: garrytan/gstack

entries.note: its GitHub search falls back to `gh auth token`, so it acts as whatever account your shell is signed in to; first-run setup installs extra command-line tools; read what each source connector needs before enabling it

entries.name: ayghri/i-have-adhd

entries.name: MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search
entries.why: Job search workflow built from coding agent skills that runs from your own copy: evaluates postings, tailors a CV, drafts cover letters and preps interviews.
entries.note: your CV and career history go to the model provider; its skills run pre-approved on your machine, so read their code first; its README warns that a fork is always public and that setup writes your name, contact details and salary expectations into tracked files, so use a private copy

entries.name: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
entries.why: Coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits whose findings are verified independently and written in a machine-readable form. Useful as a reference when checking your own review skill for gaps; adapt the ideas, not the text.

entries.name: EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
entries.why: Workflow skills for brainstorming, planning, doing and reviewing work with a coding agent; the v3.30 release notes list fixes against over-expanding a plan. Pin a commit rather than auto-updating.

entries.name: agentsmd/agents.md
entries.why: The AGENTS.md convention: one plain Markdown file of project instructions that many coding agents read, with the format's site and examples.

entries.name: petergyang/no-ai-slop
entries.why: Writing skill that removes more than twenty common patterns of machine-sounding prose while keeping the specific facts.

entries.name: rehan-remade/universal-modder
entries.why: Claude Code plugin (also usable through AGENTS.md with Codex or Cursor) for modding games: recon, engine detection, reverse engineering, building the mod, generated art, 3D and audio, in-game testing and showcase videos.
